# 0056 — The M5 demonstration

**Status:** Accepted (2026-11-03). Names settled by the owner (docs/naming.md).

## Context

M5 is done when an imported, lit scene renders the same on D3D12 and
Vulkan (image comparison), with no temporal techniques. Step 10 also
re-measures the incremental transform paths on that scene (ADR 0051), and
drops them if they save under about 5%. M4's demonstration (ADR 0046) was
a sample program run by a test, on a model we made ourselves.

## Options

**Form:** a sample and a test that runs it; or a GPU test only.

**Content:** our own, generated by a script; or a Khronos sample (Sponza,
CC-BY).

**Tolerance between backends:** strict, on one machine; or looser, allowing
for more driver differences.

**Images:** our own small PNG writer; PPM; stb_image_write (a new
dependency).

## Decision

1. **A sample game, `samples/Diorama`** (`Crucible.Samples.Diorama`),
   loaded by the launcher with `--headless --backend <api> --game …` like
   M3's Particles, and run by CTest as `samples.diorama`.
2. **Our own content:** `make_scene.py` (standard library only) writes
   one glTF per kind of object, with textures and sidecars; the script and
   its output are committed.
3. **Strict, same machine:**
   - a mean difference under 1/255, and under 0.5% of pixels off by more
     than 8/255 in any channel;
   - only Windows runs both APIs on one GPU, so the comparison runs there.
     Linux renders on Vulkan and checks the image isn't broken.
   - No golden images: GPU vendors differ in the last bits.
4. **Our own PNG writer:** uncompressed (stored deflate blocks), about 100
   lines with its reader.
5. **The incremental transform paths are dropped** (owner, after the
   measurement below): propagation recomputes every world matrix every
   run, and every matrix is uploaded every frame.

## Details

- **The models** (glTF, so the mesh importer mirrors them):
  - **Ground:** a 60 m square, its checker texture repeated 12 times (UVs
    past 4, kept as floats).
  - **House:** hard-edged walls and a gable roof (shadows, outline normals,
    a 1.2-pixel outline), a door, and blended glass windows.
  - **Tree:** a trunk and crossed, double-sided leaf cards (alpha-tested,
    alpha-to-coverage).
  - **LampPost:** a post and an emissive head (bloom).
  - **Hero:** a toon figure of spheres with a nose, outlined 2 pixels and
    tinted 30% by its surface.
  - Outlines are import settings, under `Settings` in each sidecar.
- **The scene** (`DioramaSystems.cs`, built in code):
  - four houses, six trees, four lamp posts with point lights (two
    shadowed), a shadowed spot light on the hero, an evening sun with
    cascades, a hemisphere ambient, a sky, and a camera with `PostProcess`
    (bloom 0.04, a little saturation and contrast);
  - the hero turns by a fixed amount per frame, so both APIs capture the
    same moment.
- **The game:**
  - copies its project to a temporary folder, imports it through
    `AssetDatabase`, and points `RenderAssets.SetReader` at the imported
    files. It's editor-side code in a game, which suits a demonstration.
  - Options (`--game-arg`): `project`, `frames` (8), `capture`, `compare`
    (writing `<capture>.diff.png`, the difference ×16) and `measure`.
- **Its own assemblies:** the launcher loads a game alone, from a stream,
  into its own context, and nothing finds the assemblies a game brings.
  The sample resolves its own beside the launcher's `--game` path, and
  copies its packages there (`CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies`). An engine fix
  is in docs/open-items.md.
- **The test** (`run_diorama.cmake`, labels `integration` and `gpu`):
  Vulkan, then on Windows D3D12 against the Vulkan image. Each run must
  print "Diorama: all N checks passed".

## Measured

**The comparison**, Windows, release, D3D12 against Vulkan on an RTX 2070
Super:
- mean difference 0.035/255;
- 0.110% of pixels off by more than 8/255, the largest by 138/255.
- The differences are alpha-to-coverage edges on the leaves (each driver
  maps alpha to its own sample pattern) and a faint pattern in shadowed
  walls (the shadow filter rounds slightly differently).

**The incremental transform paths**, on a town of 36 dioramas (2,776
entities, 36 heroes turning), release, 300 frames after 30 of warm-up,
medians (incremental / full):

| Machine | Frame | Propagation | Render system CPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| RX 7900 XT, Vulkan (Linux) | 0.418 / 0.421 ms | 0.046 / 0.046 ms | 0.361 / 0.366 ms |
| Again | 0.425 / 0.418 ms | 0.046 / 0.046 ms | 0.371 / 0.364 ms |
| RTX 2070 Super, D3D12 (Windows) | 1.265 / 1.194 ms | 0.114 / 0.111 ms | 1.141 / 1.070 ms |
| RTX 2070 Super, Vulkan (Windows) | 1.143 / 1.155 ms | 0.076 / 0.076 ms | 1.055 / 1.071 ms |

The differences are noise, either way, far under 5%. At step 5's 100k
synthetic instances the paths saved up to 24%, but a scene that size
isn't what the first games draw, and GPU-driven culling would replace
the uploads anyway.

## Why

A game run by the launcher shows the whole path a real game takes:
importing, model instances, the frame loop, transform propagation, and
the render system. Comparing on one machine catches API-specific bugs
without flagging honest vendor differences. Our own content needs no
license and exercises every M5 feature in one frame. Dropping the paths
removes change-version bookkeeping from two hot loops; the shadow atlas's
cache keeps its own hash, so it's unaffected.

## As built (M5 step 10)

- `samples/Diorama`:
  - `make_scene.py` and `Project/` (5 models, 2 textures, 184 KB);
  - `DioramaSettings.cs`, `DioramaSystems.cs`, `Png.cs` and
    `Dependencies.cs`.
- `samples.diorama` in `src/native/launcher/CMakeLists.txt`.
- Dropped:
  - `forceFullTransformUploads`, `DrawStats::transformsSent`, the frame
    copies' change versions, propagation's change checks, and the
    step-5 benchmark;
  - the tests now check placement and drawing, not what was skipped.
- Steam Deck measurements of shadows, bloom and outlines wait for a device
  (M10).
